## Summary

Built and verified the full persistent Chrome browser profile infrastructure on VERIDIAN-DEV for INS-20260725-054500:

- **Chrome 150.0.7871.186** installed user-space at `/opt/veridian/browser/chrome` (no root available — extracted the official `.deb` via `dpkg-deb -x`, reusing the doc-worker's existing shared-library extraction plus a small supplemental set).
- **Directory layout** `/opt/veridian/browser/{chrome,profile,downloads,uploads,cache,screenshots,recordings,temp}` created, `profile/` locked to `700` rajat-only.
- **Headless smoke test** verified end-to-end: `--dump-dom` against `https://example.com/` exits 0 with real HTML.
- **Playwright helper + smoke test** (`scripts/browser/persistent-profile.js`, `scripts/browser/smoketest.js`) reusing the *existing* Playwright install doc-worker tasks already use (`^1.62.0-alpha-1783623505000`) — no duplicate install. Real run navigated and extracted content from a live page.
- **Hardened one-time VNC login path** (`/opt/veridian/browser/vnc/`) — TigerVNC installed user-space, bound to `127.0.0.1` only, tested end-to-end (brought up, verified loopback-only listening socket, torn down, confirmed empty). Full Owner-facing procedure in `VNC_LOGIN_PROCEDURE.md`.
- **Documentation**: `ai-os/BROWSER_AUTOMATION_PROFILE_2026-07-25.yaml`, registered in `MASTER_INDEX.yaml` and knowledge_engine.
- **PR opened**: https://github.com/FChecklist/claude-control/pull/61

**No Google login was attempted** — per the hard constraint, that's exclusively the Owner's manual step. The short procedure:

1. On the server: `/opt/veridian/browser/vnc/setup-vnc.sh`
2. On your laptop: `ssh -N -L 5947:127.0.0.1:5947 rajat@<server-host>`
3. Point a VNC viewer at `127.0.0.1:5947`, enter the printed session password
4. Sign into Google (email, password, 2FA) in the Chrome window
5. Close Chrome cleanly so the profile saves
6. Close the VNC viewer/tunnel, then on the server run `/opt/veridian/browser/vnc/teardown-vnc.sh`
